Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really helped us understand Redwood's runtime. Before we move to the pilot stage, legal and security asked for a brief, plain-language confirmation of what gets kept from a sample prompt/response cycle and for how long. Can you confirm the following in writing?

1) What parts of the request/response are persisted by default (raw prompt, derived embeddings, token logs, full output, input metadata).
2) Where those persisted artifacts can reside (hosted: which regions; dedicated/private: options).
3) Default retention TTLs for each artifact type and whether TTLs are configurable per-account.
4) Controls for disabling capture of specific fields or disabling persistence entirely for certain routes.
5) Audit/logging: who can access logs, retention of access logs, and rotation/encryption details.

We also need a copy of any short compliance artifacts you can share (SOC 2 summary, redacted dataflow). If you can get us the answers and the two artifacts by EOD Wednesday (our review meeting), that would keep momentum.

Best,
Sara

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prompt outputs — PII storage specifics (post-demo)

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, itemized answer based on our hosted offering (I'll add notes for Dedicated/Private and attachments at the bottom). Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if any item needs more depth.

1) Persisted artifacts (hosted API, default):
   - Raw prompt payload: optional. By default hosted captures prompts when customer enables "capture for evals"; can be disabled at route level.
   - Model outputs (response text): short-term cache for 60s for streaming optimization, persisted only if "save_outputs" flag is true. Default hosted saves outputs for 30 days (configurable).
   - Token-level logs (metadata for billing/latency): retained 90 days by default; aggregated metrics retained longer.
   - Derived embeddings: only persisted if customer requests embeddings API and chooses to store them; not stored by default.
   - Input metadata (request time, customer route id, region): retained 365 days by default for auditability.

2) Storage locations and options:
   - Hosted: data stored in region selected at account setup (US: us-west-2 by default; EU available on request). Customers can request EU-only storage during onboarding.
   - Dedicated: customer-owned capacity in a dedicated VPC/GPU pool; persistent artifacts live in the customer-determined cloud region (we provide configuration guidance).
   - Private/on-prem: artifacts remain in customer infra — Redwood control plane can be configured to avoid storing any payloads.

3) Retention TTLs and configurability:
   - Prompts/outputs (hosted): default 30 days, configurable to as low as 0 days (no persistence) up to 2 years under contract.
   - Token logs: default 90 days, configurable with enterprise options.
   - Metadata (audit): default 365 days, configurable.
   - Embeddings: not persisted unless requested; if persisted, TTLs follow customer-configured object store lifecycle.

4) Controls to disable capture / field-level redaction:
   - Route-level flags: "capture=false" will prevent prompt/output persistence.
   - Field masking: SDK + API support for redaction rules (regex / JSON path) that strip or hash fields before storage.
   - On Hosted, we support a pre-ingest webhook to enforce redaction server-side if customers cannot change client behavior.

5) Audit/logging and security controls:
   - Access: logs and persisted artifacts are accessible only to named service accounts and customer support engineers on a least-privilege basis; access requires 2-factor and is logged.
   - Audit log retention: access logs retained 13 months by default; longer retention available for enterprise.
   - Encryption: data at rest encrypted with AES-256; keys in hosted are customer-seeded via KMS for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: I attached two short artifacts: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (high-level flow showing where artifacts land) and SOC2-summary.pdf (scope and date of last attestation).

Open questions from our side so we provide exactly what legal needs:
   - Do you need per-field TTLs (e.g., keep metadata 365d but delete outputs after 7d)?
   - Are EU-only storage and KMS key ownership requirements mandatory for the pilot?

Next step: I can send a short one-pager with toggle names and example curl flags for your engineers. Do you want that sent to procurement and your infra lead?

Thanks,

--
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[redwood.com]

Sara — looping in to confirm operational commitments and provide the one-pager. Short answers:

- Per-field TTLs: supported on hosted via route-level lifecycle policies for most artifact classes; outputs -> 7 days, metadata -> 365 days is doable without an enterprise amendment for pilots. We'll provide exact API flags in the one-pager.
- EU-only + customer-managed KMS: supported on Dedicated/Private and available for hosted under an EU-data residency addendum (requires SOW).
- SOC2 summary date: latest attest = 2028-11-30 (Type II). The SOC2-summary.pdf attached contains scope and last test period — redacted flow is included in the redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf.
